name: Labrador Current
scope: Main offshore Labrador regional branch from an OSW southern Davis Strait gate at 60 N, along Labrador and east Newfoundland, via the western Flemish Pass region to an OSW tail-of-Grand-Banks gate at 43 N. Excludes upstream Baffin/West Greenland feeder paths, Hudson Strait intrusion, inshore Avalon branch, offshore eddy excursions and downstream westward/eastward branches. Source defines regions, not exact gates or a whole-system termination.
layer: Regional upper-ocean offshore branch geography; no fixed-depth, velocity-derived core or deep western boundary axis.
time_convention: Regional naming convention from a 1984 government synthesis; not a simultaneous observation, dated model field or assertion of constant current strength.
source_locator: Hildebrand, Oceanographic Setting, Currents, printed page 11 (PDF index 12): southern Davis Strait origin, Labrador coastal flow, inshore/offshore distinction, western Flemish Pass and tail of Grand Banks. Figure 2 arrows encode velocity classes, not measured path lengths.
source_citation: Hildebrand (1984), Oceanographic Setting, in Wilson and Addison (eds.), Health of the Northwest Atlantic, Canadian government report, pp. 8-30.
coordinate_selection: OSW chooses every offshore waypoint and exact 60 N/43 N gates. Alternatives vary regional latitude endpoints. Source arrow lengths are velocity classes and are not digitized as current lengths. Shelf-break and Flemish Pass correspondence require finer verification.

alternative_routes.interpretation: Shorter OSW Davis/tail approach convention; exact limits are editorial.
Broader OSW Davis/tail approach convention; does not trace downstream branches.

scenario_rule: Three regional endpoint conventions crossed with whole-route longitude and independent endpoint latitude shifts of -0.25/0/+0.25 degrees: 81 editorial scenarios, not empirical uncertainty.
